sources.title: Dialetto fiorentino (Wikipedia it)
sources.reliability_notes: Read in full: phonology (gorgia, vowels) and the article system (i' with gemination, lo, l'), citing Vitali 2020 and Canepari. Covers little morphology.

sources.title: Dialetti toscani (Wikipedia it)
sources.reliability_notes: Read the first 100k characters: gorgia, article i', noi si va, te/tu doubling ('te tu devi fare', 'tu fa' pena'), negation 'un/'un', infinitive apocope, mi'/tu'/su', vo/fo, ENNO forms, 'icche tu fai'. Wikipedia: facts only.

sources.title: Tuscan dialect (Wikipedia en)
sources.reliability_notes: Read first 100k characters: gorgia, c/g weakening, no diphthongization (foco, bono, novo, domo), noi si + 3sg, accusative te for tu, fo/vo, infinitive apocope, Tuscan lexicon list (babbo, garbare, codesto, cencio, diaccio, punto...). Does not cover subject clitics.

sources.title: Gorgia toscana (Wikipedia it)
sources.reliability_notes: How gorgia works (k, t, p between vowels, blocked by raddoppiamento) and why spelling it is unreliable (Benedetto Dei used h).

sources.title: bischero (Vocabolario Treccani)
sources.reliability_notes: Dictionary entry: tuning peg; Tuscan colloquial 'fool'; vulgar for male genitals; etymology uncertain; derivatives bischerello, bischeretto, bischeruccio, bischeraccio. Only facts cited.

sources.title: bischero (Wikizionario)
sources.reliability_notes: Meanings (peg, cask stopper, Tuscan 'silly person', vulgar for penis), feminine bischera, idioms 'bravo bischero!', 'ha il bischero', 'non fare il bischero', synonyms, derived bischerata. Entry flagged as incomplete.

sources.title: grullo (Wikizionario)
sources.reliability_notes: Tuscan familiar adjective/noun 'silly person'; etymology unclear.

sources.title: Note linguistiche sul cinema di Leonardo Pieraccioni (in Scritti per Nicoletta Maraschio, Accademia della Crusca, 2018)
sources.reliability_notes: Read via pdftotext. Documents on transcribed film speech: i' before nouns (i' triangolo, i' ciclone, i' gatto, i' culo), subject clitic e' / l'è, negation 'un' (un volea morire, un gli facea paura), impersonal first person plural (Si va?), icche as 'bandiera fiorentina' introducing rhetorical questions, c'ha, sicche, bono bono, imperfect in -ea (volea, facea), gorgia written h (andaho), voiceless intervocalic s, interjection oh. Only short forms cited. Author as in the volume (Neri Binazzi; attribution not verified on the PDF text I read).

sources.title: Thirteen dialect words you need to know in Florence (The Local Italy)
sources.reliability_notes: Popular article: fo/vo, topini, ganzo, grullo, boncitto, chetarsi, piaccicone, ruzzare, desinare, garbare, berciare, abbozzare, ciabattone. Single words and meanings only.

sources.title: Parole toscane (La Nazione, Firenze)
sources.reliability_notes: Words: sciocco (unsalted), cannella (tap), cencio, cascare, smarimettere. 'corpi disabitati' was in the article but not used here.

sources.title: Proverbi toscani (Wikiquote it)
sources.license: CC BY-SA 4.0; the proverbs are traditional/public-domain
sources.reliability_notes: Collection of traditional Tuscan proverbs (mostly from 19th-century collections, in literary Tuscan spelling), including Florence-related sayings. Read about 200k of 225k characters.

sources.title: Modi di dire toscani (Wikiquote it)
sources.reliability_notes: Short list of 13 Tuscan sayings (andar col canzar del piombo, caricarsi di legna verde, ha la gotta alle mani, Maremma maiala!, casca come una pera cotta, sordo come una campana, pelato come il culo delle scimmie...).

sources.title: Italian profanity (Wikipedia en)
sources.reliability_notes: Maremma maiala (widely used in Tuscany), Dio bono/Dio bonino (typical of Tuscany), fava (common in Tuscany), maiala; general cazzo, stronzo, coglione, vaffanculo, culo, accidenti, porca Madonna; blasphemy common in Tuscany and Veneto.

sources.title: Bestemmia (Wikipedia it)
sources.reliability_notes: Pattern porco + divine name, mannaggia, puttana + Madonna, euphemisms (bono, especially in Tuscany; Madosca; ostrega). Used for patterns only.

sources.title: Detti, non parole! Quando il parlante riconosce la lingua
sources.author: Neri Binazzi
sources.reliability_notes: Read in full. Peer-reviewed article built on interviews of the Vocabolario del fiorentino contemporaneo (VFC): speakers' own comments on sayings still in use (capra dei pompieri, fare le calze, avere il tonchio, babbalocco, trattare come un pellaio, ma icché tu sei te?).

sources.title: Parole di Firenze dal Vocabolario del fiorentino contemporaneo (presentazione)
sources.reliability_notes: Slides of the VFC project with interview excerpts; used only to corroborate the capra dei pompieri comparison (text layout is partly garbled in extraction).

sources.title: Il significato delle parole fiorentine dalla A alla I (FlorenceCity)
sources.reliability_notes: Read in full. Local vocabulary page (letters A-I) with slang, insults and exclamations and sample sentences. Author unnamed; items only here are unverified. Slurs listed there (homophobic, ethnic) were deliberately not used.

sources.title: Vocabolario fiorentino (Parole pensate)
sources.reliability_notes: Read in full. Personal blog glossary, close in content to FlorenceCity (not treated as independent). Slurs listed there were not used.

sources.title: Proverbi e modi di dire fiorentini (LastraOnline)
sources.reliability_notes: Local-interest page with modi di dire, exclamations and a list of vulgar sayings. Only the first half of the page was read.
